provenance.boundary: This fixture carries measured historical values, their published sources, and the classical closed form. It is sealed against the blind phase and opened exactly once, after the candidate is frozen. The fit rows and the holdout rows come from different measurement scales more than a century apart; the receipt reports that mismatch rather than absorbing it, and no value here is fitted, tuned, or re-derived.

fit_source.citation: A. J. Angstrom, Recherches sur le spectre solaire (Uppsala, 1868), the four visible hydrogen wavelengths in units of 1e-10 m, quoted by J. J. Balmer in his 1885 note in exactly these figures.
fit_source.quoted_precision_note: The table is quoted to 0.01 in units of 1e-10 m, a relative resolution of about 1.5e-6 at 6562. The limiting error is not this resolution but the scale itself: Angstrom's wavelength standard was later found to be systematically in error by roughly one part in 7000 to 8000, which is a relative offset near 1.4e-4.

holdout_source.citation: Standard-air wavelengths of the next three members of the same hydrogen series, as tabulated in modern reference compilations (NIST Atomic Spectra Database, A. Kramida, Yu. Ralchenko, J. Reader and the NIST ASD Team).
holdout_source.historical_note: Balmer's 1885 note computes the next members of the series from his formula and compares them with the white-star measurements then available; those predicted members were subsequently confirmed. The holdout here is scored against modern standard-air values rather than against the 1885-era comparison figures, which is the harder test: it crosses a measurement scale as well as a prediction.
holdout_source.scale_note: Modern values are standard-air wavelengths on a modern scale. Fitting on the 1868 scale and scoring on the modern scale leaves a systematic relative offset of the order of 1e-4, which is the size of the documented error in Angstrom's standard.

provenance.modern_value_note: Modern standard-air wavelengths for the four fit rows are 6562.79, 4861.35, 4340.47 and 4101.74 in units of 1e-10 m. The blind phase is given the 1868 figures Balmer actually worked from, not these, so the exercise reproduces Balmer's information state rather than a modern one.

target.attribution: J. J. Balmer, 'Notiz uber die Spectrallinien des Wasserstoffs', Annalen der Physik und Chemie 261(5):80-87 (1885).

column_meanings.m: a bare row label running 1..7; the physically meaningful index is m + 2, the upper quantum number of the transition, which runs 3..9
column_meanings.v: the measured wavelength in units of 1e-10 m (Angstrom)

target.constant_name: B, Balmer's constant, in units of 1e-10 m
target.label: B
